'''''Echeveria setosa''''', the '''Mexican fire cracker''', is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] Crassulaceae, [[native plant|native]] to semi-desert areas of Mexico and common throughout Puebla.<ref>{{cite web |title= ECHEVERIA SETOSA |url= http://cactus.biology.dal.ca/paulC/esetosa/esetosa.html |accessdate= 2009-02-13 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100514102735/http://cactus.biology.dal.ca/paulC/esetosa/esetosa.html |archive-date= 2010-05-14 |url-status= dead }}</ref>

==Description==
''Echeveria setosa'' is an [[evergreen]] [[succulent plant|succulent]] growing to {{convert|4|cm|0|abbr=on}} high by {{convert|30|cm|0|abbr=on}} wide, with spherical rosettes of fleshy spoon-shaped leaves covered in white hairs. These white hairs, known as glochids, can cause irritation to the skin if touched. In spring it bears {{convert|30|cm|0|abbr=on}} long stalks of red flowers with yellow tips.<ref>{{cite web |title= Echeveria setosa |url= http://www.desert-tropicals.com/Plants/Crassulaceae/Echeveria_setosa.html |accessdate= 2009-02-13 |archive-date= 2019-04-30 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20190430201438/http://www.desert-tropicals.com/Plants/Crassulaceae/Echeveria_setosa.html |url-status= dead }}</ref><ref name=RHSAZ>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1405332965|pages=1136}}</ref>

==Cultivation==
''Echeveria setosa'' is cultivated as an [[ornamental plant]]. It is grown outside in subtropical climates, such as [[Southern California]]. As it requires a minimum temperature of {{convert|7|C|F|abbr=on}}, it must be grown under glass with heat in colder [[temperateness|temperate]] regions. It can be placed outside during the summer months.

==Etymology==
''Echeveria'' is named for [[Atanasio Echeverría y Godoy]], a botanical illustrator who contributed to ''Flora Mexicana''.<ref name="gledhill">Gledhill, David (2008). "The Names of Plants". Cambridge University Press. {{ISBN|9780521866453}} (hardback), {{ISBN|9780521685535}} (paperback).  pp. 149, 351</ref>

''Setosa'' means 'covered with stiff, bristly hairs'.<ref name="gledhill" />
